mainTopic: An impure hand passing impurity for קודש, other rabbinic stringencies of קודש, and the start of the stringencies of תרומה
overview: The amud opens by asking whether, for קודש, one impure hand passes impurity to someone else's hand. ריש לקיש first limits the rule to a person's own other hand. רבי יוחנן includes another person's hand, but only through the hand that touched the impurity, and only to make קודש פסול, not טמא. The גמרא proves רבי יוחנן's view from an extra line in the משנה, and reports that ריש לקיש later agreed. It then tries to show that 'לפסול אבל לא לטמא' is a dispute between תנאים, rejects a proof from a משנה in ידים, and finds the dispute in a ברייתא between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. Next, the גמרא explains the משנה's rule about eating dry food with impure hands as a case where קודש is already in a person's mouth. It also explains why an אונן and a מחוסר כפורים need טבילה before eating קודש. Finally, a new משנה begins listing ways that תרומה is stricter than קודש, starting with when an עם הארץ is trusted about the purity of wine and oil.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: not the hand of another person
steps.stepSummary: The end of ריש לקיש's statement: the rule that a hand makes the other hand impure does not apply to someone else's hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: But another person's hand, no.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last words of ריש לקיש's opinion. He limits the משנה's rule to a person's own two hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said one hand makes 'its counterpart' impure for קודש. ריש לקיש reads that narrowly: only your own second hand, not your friend's hand. This sets up the disagreement with רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The hand of another person

phrases.english: But the hand of his fellow — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes ריש לקיש's statement, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The impure hand makes only the same person's other hand impure for קודש, not someone else's hand.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: own hand or another's, through the same hand, only to disqualify
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the rule includes another person's hand. Only the hand that touched the impurity passes it on, and its effect is only to make קודש פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Whether it is his own hand or another person's hand, it must be touched by that same hand. And it only disqualifies, but does not make impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with ריש לקיש and gives his own three-part rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the rule applies to your own hand and also to a friend's hand. Second, it works only 'באותה היד,' through the hand that actually touched the impurity. Third, the result is only פסול: the קודש cannot be eaten, but it does not become טמא enough to spread impurity further.

keyTerms.meaning: With that same hand, the one that touched the impurity
To disqualify, so the item cannot be eaten but does not spread impurity
To make fully impure, able to pass impurity on

steps.confusionAlert: 'לפסול' and 'לטמא' are not the same thing. פסול means the item is ruined for eating but stops there. טמא means it becomes impure and can pass impurity further.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Whether his own hand or the hand of his fellow,
by that same hand.
phrases.notes: He means the second hand must be touched by the hand that actually touched the impurity.

phrases.english: To disqualify, but not to render impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with ריש לקיש's narrow reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An impure hand affects another person's hand too, only through the same hand, and only to make קודש פסול.

steps.title: The source: the latter clause of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי יוחנן learned this, and points to the סיפא of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where? From what the latter clause teaches: one hand makes the other impure for קודש, but not for תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי יוחנן's source and quotes a line from the end of the משנה. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted line says a hand makes its counterpart impure for קודש but not for תרומה. On its own this line proves nothing yet. The proof depends on noticing that the line seems to repeat something.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? What is the source?
The latter clause of a משנה
Its counterpart, the other hand
Sacrificial, holy food

phrases.english: From where? From the fact that it teaches in the latter clause:
For the hand renders its counterpart impure for sacrificial food,
but not for teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the textual basis of רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that another person's hand is included
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה in חגיגה

steps.title: Why repeat what the first clause already said?
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא seems unnecessary, since the רישא of the משנה already taught this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this too? The first clause already taught it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the line seems to repeat itself. This question is the engine of the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of the משנה already said a hand makes the other hand impure for קודש. A משנה does not repeat itself for no reason. So the repeated line must be teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need this too?
The first clause of a משנה

phrases.english: Why do I need this as well?
It was already taught in the first clause!
phrases.notes: The earlier part of the same משנה already said one hand makes the other impure for קודש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the quoted סיפא looks redundant.
steps.kashyaTarget: The apparent repetition in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the רישא already taught the rule, repeating it in the סיפא needs a reason.

steps.title: The extra line includes another person's hand
steps.stepSummary: The repeated line comes to teach that even someone else's hand becomes impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that it comes to include another person's hand?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. The extra line adds another person's hand, just as רבי יוחנן said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא covered a person's own two hands. The 'extra' סיפא extends the rule to a friend's hand. This supports רבי יוחנן against ריש לקיש's first view.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, must we not learn from this?
To include, to bring in

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's repeated line is not wasted. It teaches that an impure hand affects another person's hand too.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not to be concluded from this,
that it comes to include the hand of his fellow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the redundancy by giving the סיפא a new meaning.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The סיפא includes another person's hand, which supports רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: ריש לקיש changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of transmitters, ריש לקיש is quoted agreeing completely with רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש also took back his view. For רבי יונה said in the name of רבי אמי in the name of ריש לקיש: Whether his own hand or another's, by that same hand, to disqualify but not to make impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that ריש לקיש retracted and accepted רבי יוחנן's whole rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quote from ריש לקיש uses the exact words of רבי יוחנן. So the dispute ends: both agree that another's hand is included, only through the same hand, and only to make it פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: He retracted, changed his mind

steps.whyThisMatters: Once ריש לקיש retracts, רבי יוחנן's rule stands without a dispute between them.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish, too, retracted,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָה אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי
phrases.english: for Rabbi Yona said that Rabbi Ami said
that Reish Lakish said:
Whether his own hand or the hand of his fellow,
by that same hand,
to disqualify but not to render impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the original opponent now agrees with רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש agrees: another's hand is included, only through the same hand, and only to make it פסול.

steps.title: 'Disqualify but not make impure' is a dispute of תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the idea of 'לפסול אבל לא לטמא' is debated among the תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'to disqualify but not to make impure' is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes an observation and then tries to prove it from a משנה. That proof is rejected in Step 11, and Step 12 brings the source that does show it. This line sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The agreed rule says the hand only makes קודש פסול. The גמרא now says not every תנא would agree. Some hold the hand's impurity is stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: And 'to disqualify but not to render impure'
is a dispute of tanna'im.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִפְסוֹל אֲבָל לֹא לְטַמֵּא תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places the agreed rule inside an older dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether the hand only disqualifies or truly makes impure is debated by תנאים.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: a hand makes the other hand impure
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in ידים: anything that disqualifies תרומה makes hands שניות, and one hand makes the other impure, according to רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: Anything that disqualifies תרומה makes the hands impure as second degree, and one hand makes the other impure. These are the words of רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to show the dispute. This step gives רבי יהושע's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hands that touch something which disqualifies תרומה become שניות, impure in the second degree. רבי יהושע adds that such a hand makes the other hand impure. So for him the hand's impurity actually spreads, which goes beyond 'only פסול'.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that disqualifies תרומה by touching it
Impure in the second degree

phrases.english: As we learned: Anything that disqualifies teruma
renders the hands impure to be second degree,
and a hand renders its counterpart impure,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That 'לפסול אבל לא לטמא' is debated
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מסכת ידים, the opinion of רבי יהושע

steps.title: The Rabbis: a second degree cannot make another second degree
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say hands are שניות, and a שני cannot create another שני in חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Rabbis say: Hands are second degree, and a second degree does not make another second degree in non-sacred food.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the other side of the משנה. The חכמים limit how far the hand's impurity spreads.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, the hands are only שניות, and a שני cannot make something else a שני in חולין. So they deny רבי יהושע's claim that one hand makes the other hand a שני. Whether the hand passes on any weaker impurity is not stated here: Step 10 tries to read it that way, and Step 11 rejects that reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, the majority opinion
Impure in the second degree
Ordinary, non-sacred food

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא wants to read the רבי יהושע / חכמים dispute as the 'לפסול אבל לא לטמא' question. Step 11 rejects that reading, and Step 12 brings the real source for the dispute.

phrases.english: But the Rabbis say:
Hands are second degree,
and a second degree does not make a second degree in non-sacred food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view in the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That 'לפסול אבל לא לטמא' is debated
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מסכת ידים, the opinion of the חכמים

steps.title: Reading the חכמים as saying the hand makes a third
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the חכמים only deny that the hand becomes a שני, but agree it becomes a שלישי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't this mean: it does not make a second degree, but it does make a third degree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the words of the חכמים from the previous step closely. It suggests they only said the hand does not make a שני, which hints that it does make a שלישי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this reading is right, the argument between רבי יהושע and the חכמים is exactly the 'disqualify but not make impure' question from Step 7. For רבי יהושע, the second hand makes קודש impure. For the חכמים, it is only a שלישי, so it can only disqualify.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Isn't it that...?' The גמרא is suggesting a way to read a source.
Third degree of impurity
Makes, produces

phrases.english: What, is it not [that]
it is a second degree that it does not make,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the first impure hand, and what it acts on is the other hand.

phrases.english: but a third degree it does make.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of the חכמים in Step 9
steps.raayaObject: That 'disqualify but not make impure' is debated by רבי יהושע and the חכמים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of the חכמים: a שני cannot make a שני

steps.title: Maybe the hand makes nothing at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that reading. The חכמים may hold the hand passes no impurity at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it makes neither a second nor a third.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the reading from Step 10. Maybe the חכמים hold that one hand does not make the other hand impure at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'a שני cannot make a שני' do not prove that it makes a שלישי. They may simply mean it makes nothing. So the argument may be about whether the hand passes on impurity at all, not about which level.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps

phrases.english: Perhaps it makes neither a second degree
nor a third degree.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא לָא שֵׁנִי עָבֵיד וְלָא שְׁלִישִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of Step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה in ידים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wording of the חכמים does not have to mean they agree the hand makes a שלישי

steps.title: The real argument is between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finds a clear source: רבי says the second hand makes קודש impure, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says it only disqualifies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like these תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: a dry hand makes the other hand impure, so that it makes קודש impure but not תרומה. These are the words of רבי. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: that hand can disqualify, but not make impure.
steps.whatsHappening: After the proof from ידים fell apart, the גמרא brings a ברייתא where the argument from Step 7 is stated clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds the second hand is strong enough to make קודש truly impure, so the food can pass impurity on. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds it can only disqualify the קודש, so the food cannot spread impurity further. This is exactly the 'לפסול אבל לא לטמא' argument.

keyTerms.meaning: תנאים, the sages of the משנה era
Dry
Its fellow, here the other hand
To disqualify, making it unfit without letting it spread impurity

steps.whatToRemember: The 'disqualify but not make impure' argument is between רבי (makes impure) and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה (only disqualifies).

phrases.english: Rather, it is like these תנאים,
as it was taught in a ברייתא:
A dry hand makes its fellow hand impure
so that it makes impure with קודש,
but not with תרומה,
these are the words of רבי.
רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says:
that hand can disqualify,
but not make impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof with a clear ברייתא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The argument from Step 7 is between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about eating dry food with impure hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה: dry foods may be eaten with impure hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may eat dry foods with impure hands, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting our משנה. It is setting up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food only becomes able to take on impurity after it gets wet. The משנה allows eating dry food with impure hands for תרומה, but not for קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Dry foods, which never got wet and so cannot become impure
Impure

phrases.english: One may eat dry foods
with impure hands, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' points to the rest of the משנה line: this is allowed for תרומה but not for קודש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dry foods may be eaten with impure hands (for תרומה, not קודש).

steps.title: Can קודש food ever count as 'dry'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס asks how קודש can be 'dry', since its preciousness makes it able to become impure anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס said: Is there such a thing as 'dry' for קודש? Doesn't the preciousness of קודש make it able to become impure?
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא challenges the משנה. For קודש, it makes no difference whether the food is dry, so why mention dryness at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normal food needs to get wet before it can become impure. קודש is so precious that it can become impure even without getting wet. So the משנה's line about 'dry' food seems to make no difference for קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: The preciousness of קודש
Makes them able to become impure, like getting wet does
But isn't it so that...?

steps.confusionAlert: Here מכשיר does not mean 'kosher'. It means making food able to become impure.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא:
רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס said:
Is there such a thing as 'dry' for קודש?
Doesn't the preciousness of קודש make them able to become impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's mention of dry food, which seems to matter for קודש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קודש can become impure without getting wet, so dryness should make no difference.

steps.title: The case is food already in his mouth
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is not about dry קודש. It is about קודש or תרומה that got into a person's mouth without his hands touching it. Now he wants to add plain radish or onion with his impure hands. The Rabbis forbade this for קודש but not for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the line is needed. The case is where his friend put the food into his mouth, or he put it in himself using a spindle or whorl, and then he wanted to eat a חולין radish or onion along with it. For קודש the Rabbis made a decree; for תרומה they did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 14 by explaining that the משנה is talking about a different case than we first thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that קודש can never count as 'dry', so the משנה's case could not be about dry קודש. The answer changes the case. The קודש reached his mouth without his hands touching it, and his hands now touch only plain חולין food. The Rabbis still worried he might touch the קודש in his mouth, so they made a גזירה for קודש only.

keyTerms.meaning: 'No, it is needed.' The line is needed for a different case.
Put in, stuck in
Spindle and whorl, wooden tools that cannot become impure
The Rabbis made a protective decree
Ordinary food that is not holy

steps.confusionAlert: His hands never touch the קודש here. The problem is only the worry that while eating the radish he might touch the קודש that is in his mouth.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how far the Rabbis went to protect קודש. They even worried about indirect contact with food in the mouth, and they did not go that far for תרומה.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary,

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁתָּחַב לוֹ חֲבֵירוֹ לְתוֹךְ פִּיו,
phrases.english: for example, where his friend put [the food] into his mouth,
or where he put it in himself
with a spindle or a whorl,
phrases.notes: These are wooden spinning tools that can't become impure, so the food gets into his mouth without becoming impure.

phrases.english: and he wanted to eat
a non-sacred radish or onion along with them.
For קודש, the Rabbis made a decree about them;
for תרומה, the Rabbis did not make a decree about them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, כְּגוֹן שֶׁתָּחַב לוֹ חֲבֵירוֹ לְתוֹךְ פִּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס by redefining the משנה's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה was about dry קודש touched by impure hands, which cannot be, since קודש is always able to become impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is קודש already in the mouth while impure hands touch only חולין food. The Rabbis decreed against this for קודש but not for תרומה.

steps.title: Why do the אונן and מחוסר כפורים need immersion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about the אונן and the מחוסר כפורים, and asks for the reason behind the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The אונן and one lacking atonement, etc.' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks why it gives this rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says these people need טבילה before eating קודש, though not for תרומה. Neither of them is actually impure, so the גמרא wants to know why immersion is required.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner on the day a close relative died
Someone who has finished purifying but has not yet brought his atonement קרבן
What is the reason?

phrases.english: An acute mourner and one lacking atonement, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' points to the rest of the משנה's line: they need immersion for קודש but not for תרומה.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹנֵן וּמְחוּסַּר כִּפּוּרִים כּוּ׳. מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why do people who are not impure need טבילה before eating קודש?

steps.title: They were not careful until now
steps.stepSummary: Until now they were not allowed to eat קודש, so they may not have guarded themselves from impurity. That is why the Rabbis required טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since until now they were forbidden to eat it, the Rabbis required them to immerse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question and gives the reason for the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While someone is forbidden to eat קודש, he has no reason to be careful about טומאה. Now that he is allowed to eat it again, the Rabbis worried he might have become impure without noticing. So they required טבילה as a safety measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Until now
They required them
Immersion in a מקוה

steps.whatToRemember: The טבילה of the אונן and מחוסר כפורים is a rabbinic safety measure. It exists because they had no reason to watch their purity while they were not allowed to eat קודש.

phrases.english: Since until now they were forbidden [to eat קודש],
the Rabbis required them to immerse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They may not have guarded themselves from טומאה while they were not allowed to eat קודש, so the Rabbis required טבילה.

steps.title: New משנה: where תרומה is stricter
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists ways that תרומה is treated more strictly than קודש. First case: in יהודה, everyone is trusted about the purity of wine and oil of קודש all year, but about תרומה only at pressing time.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a stringency in תרומה: in יהודה people are trusted about the purity of wine and oil all year long, and during the season of the winepress and olive press, even about תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It turns the earlier list around and starts listing cases where תרומה is stricter than קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even an עם הארץ is trusted about the purity of קודש wine and oil all year. For תרומה he is trusted only during pressing season. That makes תרומה the stricter one here, the opposite of the earlier list.

keyTerms.meaning: A new משנה begins
A stringency that applies to תרומה
Are trusted
Winepresses and olive presses (the pressing season)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think תרומה is holier than קודש. קודש is holier. Here the trust rules simply happen to be easier for קודש.

phrases.english: MISHNA: There is a stringency in תרומה,
that in יהודה [all people] are trusted
about the purity of wine and oil
phrases.notes: He means wine and oil of קודש, as the next line's contrast with תרומה shows.

phrases.english: all the days of the year,
and during the time of the winepresses and olive presses,
even about תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה that reverses the direction of the previous list of חומרות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In יהודה, people are trusted about the purity of קודש wine and oil all year, but about תרומה only during pressing season.

steps.title: After pressing season, a barrel of תרומה is turned away unless it holds some קודש
steps.stepSummary: Once pressing season is over, a careful כהן may not accept a barrel of תרומה wine from an עם הארץ. The barrel may be kept until the next pressing season. If the giver says he put a רביעית of קודש into it, he is trusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the winepresses and olive presses are finished, if someone brings a careful כהן a barrel of תרומה wine, the כהן should not take it. The giver may hold it until next year's pressing time. But if the giver says, 'I put a רביעית of קודש into it,' he is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its first case. It tells us what happens to תרומה wine brought after pressing time, when an עם הארץ is no longer trusted about תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עם הארץ is trusted about תרומה only at pressing time, so after that the כהן must refuse the barrel. The same barrel becomes acceptable at the next pressing season, when he is trusted again. Since he is trusted about קודש all year, once the barrel has קודש mixed in, he is believed about the whole barrel.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary person who is not careful about purity laws
Winepresses and olive presses, meaning the pressing season
A barrel
The next pressing season
A quarter of a לוג, a small amount of liquid
Trusted, believed

steps.confusionAlert: The barrel itself does not change. It is refused now but accepted next pressing season only because the trust given to the עם הארץ changes with the season.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows clearly how תרומה is stricter than קודש: the trust for קודש lasts all year, while the trust for תרומה lasts only during pressing time.

phrases.english: Once the winepresses and olive presses have passed,

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵבִיאוּ לוֹ חָבִית שֶׁל יַיִן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה
phrases.english: and they brought him a barrel of תרומה wine,
phrases.notes: 'They' means ordinary people who are not careful about purity, and 'him' is a careful כהן.

phrases.english: he should not accept it from him,
but he may leave it for the next pressing season.
And if he said to him:
I separated into it a quarter-לוג of קודש,
he is trusted.
phrases.notes: He is believed about the whole barrel, because he is trusted about קודש all year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the first case of the משנה begun in step 18, explaining what happens outside pressing time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After pressing season, a careful כהן may not accept תרומה wine from an עם הארץ. The giver may keep it until the next season. If he says קודש was mixed in, he is trusted.

steps.title: The משנה begins a new case about jugs of wine and oil
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens its next case with the words 'jugs of wine and jugs of oil.' The rule itself comes in the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Jugs of wine and jugs of oil...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The משנה names the subject of its next case, and the actual rule continues right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After finishing the barrel case, the משנה moves on to jugs of wine and oil. Nothing has been ruled yet. We only know that the next rule is about these jugs.

keyTerms.meaning: Jugs, clay containers for wine or oil

phrases.english: Jugs of wine and jugs of oil

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the barrel case to the next case in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the subject is named here (jugs of wine and oil). The ruling continues in the next part.
